summary: Model resolution tests pass, but preflight cannot persist its model state or reliably determine installed role tiers; init also has integrity and recovery defects. Full suite timed out after 120 seconds.

findings.summary: Provide a state-writer operation for recording resolved models
findings.evidence: Preflight instructs the orchestrator to record and later overwrite models, but the new CLI dispatch only adds read-only models and project init; no run-state command writes this field. state.md:170 and ADR 0006 prohibit manual state edits, and cmd_resume only records status and history. Therefore new selections cannot be persisted through the permitted interface, and resume cannot compare or update them as required by FR-005 and FR-009. ENG-15 and ENG-26 require an operation preserving the state contract.
findings.fix: Add a locked, validated state-writer operation for model resolution, including pending and worktree runs and resume delta reporting; call it from preflight and test both lifecycle paths.

findings.summary: Make each role's tier available to the installed orchestrator
findings.evidence: FR-006 requires selecting the resolved model for every role's tier, but the instruction supplies no role-to-tier mapping. tools/render.py:241-242 installs role bodies without their frontmatter, which is where core/roles/*.md declares tier; rendered agent frontmatter at tools/render.py:124-162 also omits the tier. The installed skill thus has no authoritative tier mapping for choosing deep versus standard, and can select the wrong model for a role. ENG-15 requires an explicit usable contract.
findings.fix: Ship a single authoritative role-to-tier mapping with the installed skill or preserve accessible tier metadata, and instruct preflight/spawn to use it; verify all rendered roles map to their authored tier.

findings.summary: Prevent concurrent init from overwriting an existing project configuration
findings.evidence: ENG-26 and FR-014 require preserving an existing config. The exists check at lines 90-91 is separate from os.replace at line 119; if another init or user creates config.json after the check, replace silently overwrites that new file. Atomic replacement does not provide no-clobber semantics.
findings.fix: Publish the completed temporary config with an atomic no-replace operation or use an appropriate lock/exclusive creation protocol, and report a competing creation as a refusal.

findings.summary: Avoid leaving init permanently half-complete when README creation fails
findings.evidence: ENG-17 and ENG-26 require deliberate handling of partial failures. Init publishes config.json before attempting config.README.md; if the README destination is a directory, os.replace raises IsADirectoryError after config creation, prints a traceback, and every retry refuses because config.json now exists. The same unrecoverable partial result can follow an I/O failure during the second write, violating FR-013's two-file bootstrap.
findings.fix: Stage both outputs and handle publication failures so a failed init remains recoverable without deleting a user's configuration; surface a concise diagnostic and add a failure-path test.
